newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: UNIONS ANGRY OVER TELSTRA'S PLANNED JOB CUTS

Unions have expressed anger over plans by Telstra to shed another 22,000 jobs over the next three years. The Communications Union and the Telecommunications division of the Community and Public Sector Union say the cuts are driven by the Government's privatisation agenda.
They say the size of Telstra's profit demonstrates the absurdity of the privatisation plans, saying the Government wants to sell the goose that lays the golden eggs.
ALSTON SAYS NO GUARANTEES FOR JOBS FOR TELSTRA WORKERS
Communications Minister Richard Alston says while many redundant Telstra workers will find jobs in the private sector, there's no guarantees.

Telstra has announced a profit of A$2.3 billion for the past financial year, a A$500 million boost on the previous year. Telstra's boost in profits and planned expansion will come at a cost of a further 22,000 job losses over the next three years. Senator Alston has welcomed Telstra's profit, and says the earmarked job losses are all part of boosting the carrier's efficiency.
LETTER CALLS FOR WITHDRAWAL FROM BOUGAINVILLE
A letter calling for the withdrawal of PNG troops from Bougainville has been presented to the annual talks between the Australian and Papua New Guinea governments underway in Adelaide.
Representatives of the Bougainville Interim Government have presented the letter to Australia's Foreign Affairs Minister, Alexander Downer, and PNG's Deputy Prime Minister, Chris Haiveta.
The letter also calls for moves to start new peace talks with Bougainville rebels, and the suspension of all Australian aid to PNG until peace is restored on the island.
THREE LEGGED KANGAROO
A three-legged kangaroo has been found near Port Augusta in South Australia, and scientists are having trouble thinking of a name for him.
His abnormality was noticed when highway patrol workers stopped to help the injured animal.
Environmental scientist Doug Reilly says the three-legged roo has a fully-formed leg growing between the others.
Mr Reilly says the kangaroo's third leg will be amputated so that he can get around more easily.
BANK WORKERS CONCERNED ABOUT JOB LOSSES
The Finance Sector Union has called on the Wallis Inquiry into Australia's financial system to consider the affect continued mergers are having on bank employees.
It wants the inquiry to give equal weight to the affect of mergers on staff, as well as consumers and shareholders.
The union says the most important consideration in whether mergers should be allowed in future should be job losses among bank staff.
NUDE BEACH CREATES DILEMMA IN QUEENSLAND
The Queensland Government's new National Park charge may create a dilemma for some visitors.
The State Opposition has questioned where visitors to a Sunshine Coast nudist beach will pin their passes.
Environment Minister Brian Littleproud told Parliament he hoped Deputy Opposition Leader Jim Elder didn't have a personal interest in the beach.

Mr Littleproud says people wanting to visit the beach would be able to buy a pass - confirming checks would be carried out which led the Opposition to suggest a check might have to involve a bodysearch.
HINDMARSH ISLAND ROW
The Federal Opposition says the Government would be in breach of the Racial Discrimination Act if it tries to change the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Heritage Protection Act.

A spokeswoman for Aboriginal Affairs Minister, John Herron, has refused to comment on a newspaper report that the Government might amend the act to avoid calling a further inquiry into the Hindmarsh Island Bridge.
Labor Aboriginal Affairs Spokesman, Daryl Melham, says amending the act would be a breach of the Racial Discrimination Act.
Mr Melham says the Government should not seek a quick fix by trying to take away people's rights.
